SUBJECT: Reclassify and Amend Unclassified Use Permit (UUP) No. 46 as Conditional Use Permit
(CUP) No. 26-04.

PROJECT PROPOSAL/REQUEST: A request for a reclassification and amendment to Unclassified Use
Permit (UUP) No.46 to Conditional Use Permit (CUP) NO.26-04 to allow modifications of an existing
monopine wireless telecommunications facility, including the removal, replacement, and reconfiguration
of antennas, remote radio heads, and associated support equipment, located at 9611 Pinehurst Avenue
(South Gate Park).

Project Overview

•  General Plan Designation: Park/ Plaza/ Open Space

•  Zoning: Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan (TBSP); Open Space (OS)

•  Project Location: 9611 Pinehurst Avenue

•  Assessor’s Parcel Number: 6222-023-900

•  Applicant: John McDonald, on behalf of EukonGroup / “Agent for AT&T”

BACKGROUND:

Project Overview: The subject site is located within South Gate Park at 9611 Pinehurst Avenue and is
developed with an existing wireless telecommunications facility designed as a monopine. The facility is
situated within the interior of the approximately 96-acre public park, which contains a variety of
recreational amenities, including athletic fields, playgrounds, picnic areas, community buildings, and
parking facilities. The monopine is designed to resemble a pine tree to minimize visual impacts and is
accompanied by associated ground-mounted equipment located within a secured equipment enclosure.

The wireless facility was originally approved on August 9, 2005, when City Council adopted Resolution
No. 7067 approving unclassified Use Permit N0.46, which authorized the installation and operation of a
new wireless communications facility consisting of a monopine and prefabricated equipment shelter.
Subsequently, on May 25, 2010, City Council adopted Resolution No. 7369 approving Unclassified Use
Permit No.67, which authorized the collocation of a wireless telecommunications facility consisting of a
nine panel antennas mounted on the existing monopine, along with four equipment cabinets located within
the existing facility footprint.

The proposed project is limited to modifications of the existing wireless telecommunications facility,
including the replacement, relocation, and reconfiguration of antennas, remote radio heads, and associated
support equipment, as well as upgrades to the existing power and battery systems. No expansion of the

Surroundings: The project site is bounded generally by residential neighborhoods to the north, south, east,

Pinehurst Avenue is located along the western edge of the park, while various internal drive aisles, parking
areas, and recreational facilities provide access throughout the site. The surrounding development pattern
is predominantly residential in character, consisting primarily of single-family homes, with public and
institutional uses associated with the park and nearby civic facilities.

ANALYSIS:

•  Municipal Code Requirements for a UUP: Pursuant to the former South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC)
  Section 11.26.010, (10.5), microwave installations with any tower or receiver extending more than six
  feet in height and not enclosed within a building were required to obtain an Unclassified Use Permit.
  At that time, approval of a UUP also required review and approval by the City Council.

•  In 2015, the City adopted a comprehensive update to the Zoning Code, which removed former SGMC
  Section 11.26 and repurposed the chapter as the Corridor Transition Overlay. During this update, the
  provisions governing Unclassified Use Permits were not incorporated into another section of the
  Municipal Code. Therefore, Staff believes it is appropriate to reclassify the existing UUP as a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP), as the CUP entitlement most closely reflects the purpose and regulatory
  intent of the former UUP process.

•  Required findings for a CUP: Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the
  Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as
  applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the
  existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

CUP Analysis

In granting approval of a CUP, the Planning Commission shall make all the following findings, as
applicable to the property, as found in SGMC Section 11.52.030.

A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of this title
  or the City’s General Plan. The proposed project consists of modifications to an existing AT&T wireless
  telecommunications facility through the replacement and reconfiguration of antennas, remote radio
  heads, and associated support equipment to improve network reliability, capacity, and service quality.
  The project is consistent with the South Gate General Plan Community Design Element, including Goal

  The project is also consistent with the vision and purpose of the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan

  businesses, and create a vibrant destination within South Gate. Modern wireless communications
  infrastructure supports these objectives by providing the technological services necessary for
  businesses, visitors, and community members to access mobile communications, internet-based
  services, and emergency response systems. Because the project modernizes an existing facility without
  expanding its footprint or altering its visual character, approval of the CUP supports the
  implementation of the General Plan and TBSP while preserving the established development pattern
  of the area.

B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the existing
  and future land uses of the applicable zone. The proposed modifications are limited to equipment
  upgrades within an existing stealth monopine facility located within South Gate Park. The project does
  not propose an increase in the height of the monopine, expansion of the lease area, or changes to the
  overall operation of the facility. As a result, the facility will continue to function as an unobtrusive
  utility use that is compatible with the surrounding recreational, commercial, and residential uses.

  The project advances the goals of the Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan (TBSP) by supporting continued
  investment in infrastructure that serves the surrounding community while maintaining the area's
  character and sense of place. The TBSP emphasizes creating an attractive, functional, and
  economically sustainable district that serves residents and visitors. Reliable wireless service is an
  essential component of a modern commercial corridor and supports businesses, customers, and public
  gathering spaces within the TBSP area. Because the existing monopine design will remain intact and
  all improvements are confined to the existing facility footprint, the project remains compatible with
  both existing and future land uses envisioned by the General Plan and TBSP.

C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the character
  or function of the neighborhood. The proposed project will not generate additional traffic, parking
  demand, noise, lighting, or other operational impacts beyond those associated with the existing facility.
  The modifications consist primarily of replacing and upgrading telecommunications equipment
  necessary to improve wireless coverage and network performance. No expansion of the facility's
  physical footprint, increase in height, or substantial exterior modifications are proposed.

  The Tweedy Boulevard Specific Plan (TBSP) identifies the enhancement of community amenities,
  improvement of the public realm, and creation of a vibrant and functional environment as key objectives
  for the corridor. Reliable telecommunications infrastructure directly supports these objectives by
  facilitating communication, commerce, public safety, and access to services throughout the community.
  Furthermore, the retention of the existing stealth monopine design minimizes visual impacts and
  preserves the character of South Gate Park and the surrounding neighborhood. Therefore, the
  proposed CUP would not be detrimental to adjacent properties and would support the continued
  function of the neighborhood and TBSP area through the modernization of existing public utility
  infrastructure.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS:

In accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project qualifies for a
categorical exemption under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, as the
proposed project consist of minor alterations to an existing wireless telecommunications facility, including
the removal, replacement, and reconfiguration of antennas, remote radio heads, and associated support
equipment, as well as upgrades to existing power and battery systems. The project involves negligible
expansion of the existing use and will occur within the existing facility footprint.

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION:

Advertising and notification of the public hearing for the application were conducted in compliance with
Chapter 11.50.020, Title 11 of the South Gate Municipal Code. Notice of the hearing was originally posted
and published in the “South Gate Press” newspaper and was mailed to surrounding properties on June 25,
2026.

CONCLUSION:

Based on the above analysis, Staff has determined that with the recommended conditions of approval, the
proposed project will comply with the SGMC, and all the required findings in support of a CUP
reclassification and amendment will be made.

RECOMMENDATION:

Based on the evidence presented, Staff recommends that the Planning Commission find that the project is
Categorically Exempt from the CEQA under Section 15301, (Class 1) “Existing Facilities”, make the
required findings and requirements set forth in the South Gate Municipal Code, and approve the application
to reclassify and amend Unclassified Use Permit (UUP) No.46 to Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No.26-
04, subject to the conditions of approval contained in the attached Resolution No. 2026-08 and/or other
conditions that the Planning Commission may wish to impose.

establish a rental car business with ancillary car wash services for the rental fleet within an existing

BACKGROUND:

•  Site Characteristics: The subject site is located at 3705 Firestone Boulevard and is developed with an
  existing one-story commercial building situated on a parcel measuring approximately 15,000 square
  feet. The property is located along the northerly side of Firestone Boulevard, a major commercial
  corridor within the City of South Gate characterized by a mix of retail, service, and automotive-oriented
  uses. The site is improved with surface parking areas that provide access from Firestone Boulevard and
  San Carlos Avenue.

•  Surroundings: The subject site is surrounded by a fully urbanized environment, characterized by the
  existing commercial developments, such as retail stores, restaurants, professional offices, automotive
  sales establishments, vehicle repair facilities, and other neighborhood-serving businesses. Properties
  along Firestone Boulevard are generally developed with one-story commercial buildings and associated
  surface parking, reflecting the established commercial nature of the corridor. Residential
  neighborhoods are located north of the corridor and are separated from Firestone Boulevard by
  intervening commercial development.

•  Project Description: The proposed project consists of the tenant improvement and adaptive reuse of an
  existing 4,159-square-foot commercial building located at 3705 Firestone Boulevard for operation as
  an Enterprise Rent-A-Car facility with an ancillary indoor vehicle wash and detailing area. The project
  will retain the existing building footprint while undertaking interior and exterior renovations, including

ANALYSIS:

•  Municipal Code Requirements for a CUP: Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section
  11.21.030, Table 11.21-3 (Allowed Land Uses, Urban Mixed-Use Zones), the rental of vehicles and
  washing/ detailing of vehicles may be permitted provided a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) is granted
  by the Planning Commission.

•  Required findings for a CUP: Pursuant to SGMC Section 11.52.030, before a CUP may be granted, the
  Planning Commission (or the City Council on appeal) shall make all the following findings, as
  applicable to the property:

  A. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose of
  this title or the city’s General Plan.

  B. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible with the
  existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.

  C. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to the
  character or function of the neighborhood.

Business Operations

services, and related administrative functions. The applicant indicates that a significant portion of customers
will utilize Enterprise’s complimentary pick-up and delivery service, which transports customers between
their homes, hotels, insurance offices, or vehicle repair facilities and the rental office. This operational

vehicles and will not be operated as a stand-alone commercial car wash or be open to the general public.
No customer vehicles or third-party vehicles will be washed, detailed, serviced, or stored on the premises.

To ensure compatibility with surrounding properties, staff recommends conditions of approval requiring all
vehicle washing and detailing activities to be conducted entirely within the enclosed building, prohibiting

maintenance of all landscaping, parking facilities, lighting, fencing, and building improvements in good
condition to ensure the continued orderly operation of the site and compatibility with the surrounding
commercial corridor.

250 square feet of gross floor area. As such, a 1,458 square-foot office area will require a total of six (6)

being dedicated to customer parking, and the remaining 11 parking spaces are utilized for inventory storage.
Furthermore, there are four (4) enclosed tandem parking spaces within the existing commercial building

  or the City’s General Plan. The proposed Enterprise Rent-A-Car facility is consistent with the South
  Gate General Plan Community Design Element for the Firestone Corridor, which recognizes the
  corridor as a predominantly commercial and auto-oriented area containing vehicle sales, repair, and
  related automotive uses. The project reoccupies and renovates an existing commercial building without
  expanding the building footprint, thereby contributing to the revitalization of an aging commercial
  corridor consistent with the Firestone Corridor Vision, which seeks to transform the corridor through
  reinvestment, property improvements, and the enhancement of existing commercial properties.
  Additionally, Firestone Corridor Policy P.2 encourages single-use commercial development when
  appropriate, provided it does not detract from the overall character of the corridor, while Policy P.1
  encourages commercial uses that capitalize on the corridor’s regional accessibility and economic
  activity.

reasonable possibility that the activity will have a significant effect on the environment due to unusual

Based on the above analysis, staff has determined that with the recommended conditions of approval, the
